note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Columbia beat its own revenue guidance and consensus in both reported 2026 quarters. Q1 revenue was $779.0m vs a $755.6m consensus, with EPS $0.65 vs $0.35. Q2 revenue was $614.4m vs ~$607m. Consensus for Q3 ($938-942.5m, EPS $1.25-1.28) sits at the top of the $929-943m revenue guide and the middle of the $1.15-1.35 EPS guide. Management said the >$30m Q3-to-Q4 shift is timing, 'not a function of any cancellations', and that there were 'no changes in our order book for fall 2026'. A modest beat on the quarter is the base case, at about +1% revenue vs bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 beat with raised op-income guide: +2.35%. Q2 2026 beat on revenue with a soft Q3 guide: -5.43%. 5 of the last 7 prints fell, so this name has not reliably paid for quarterly beats.

findings.finding: Input costs worsened after the July guide. On the Q2 call the CFO flagged incremental outbound freight charges and fuel pressure, and cited oil 'in the $90-$100 range' as a fall 2027 headwind. Brent has held above $100 since late September ($103.50 on Oct 12), and the EIA's October outlook puts Q4 2026 Brent at $104.69. Tanker freight stays elevated after strikes near Hormuz. This raises the risk that the H2 margin guide (FY op margin 8.5-9.3%) is trimmed or that the early 2027 margin commentary is cautious.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (EIA October STEO; URL path undated, content refers to the Q4 2026 forecast)
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: 'H2 outlook incrementally moderated' plus a Q3 guide below the Street gave -5.43%. Q2 2025 (2025-07-31): -12.85% on a weak outlook. Guidance cuts have been punished hard.

findings.finding: NOAA's 2026-27 Winter Outlook (Oct 16) projects a very strong El Nino with warmer-than-average temperatures across much of the northern US for Dec-Feb. This lands on the quarter Columbia's guide leans on. The FY guide implies Q4 sales of about $1.09-1.18bn: FY $3.43-3.50bn less Q1 $779.0m, Q2 $614.4m and the Q3 guide. That is roughly +6% at the midpoint including the >$30m shifted shipments, against about 4-5% underlying per the CFO. CEO Boyle on the Q2 call: 'the weather tends to be much more impactful than almost any economic indicator.' A cautious Q4 framing or a FY sales trim is the risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 outlook prints: 2025-10-30 -3.63% and 2025-07-31 -12.85% on weak outlooks. Feb 2026 +14.44% when the FY26 guide surprised up. The guide moves this name more than the quarter does.

findings.finding: A direct outerwear peer reported on Oct 28, after Columbia last spoke. VF's The North Face grew 4% in the quarter to Sep 26, with Americas +8%. Timberland Americas grew +15%. Americas ex-Dickies grew +6% 'reflecting sustained growth across channels'. VF guided TNF Q3 (Oct-Dec) to +4% or better, said it feels 'really, really good about Q3, Q4', and built inventory +7% 'to support demand in H2'. That is evidence that US outdoor/outerwear wholesale and DTC demand held through September. It supports Columbia's guided return to US wholesale growth in H2, weighted to Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No COLM-specific history on peer reads. COLM's US business fell 4% in Q2 and 8% in H1 while TNF Americas grew 8% in H1, so Columbia has been losing share. The read-through is weaker than a like-for-like.
